annotations.title: A video in each place's shape

description: Use it when the user wants a video for TikTok, Reels, Shorts, YouTube, X or LinkedIn: vertical, square or 4:5, or cut to a place's length or size. Turns one finished video into the version each place takes, with ffmpeg on this machine: 9:16 for TikTok, Reels and Shorts, 4:5 for the feeds, 1:1, and 16:9 for YouTube, X and LinkedIn. In each shot the crop follows what moves, not faces, and a shot whose action or words are wider than the crop is padded, shown whole on a blurred copy of itself. Each file is cut at a shot change to its place's length, kept under its size limit, set to the loudness asked for, given a cover beside it and checked against the limits the place publishes. FORMATS.md, which the result shows, lists every file with its checks; sheet.png, the picture to show first, draws each shape's window on every shot. A launch film's timeline or a demo's steps file beside the video gives its shots. To move a window, plan first and edit crop.json. For a look at the windows before anything renders, use plan_reframe instead. The reframe playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (reframekit 0.1.4, on this machine.)

brand.description: A brand kit, its folder, brand.json or _brand.yml: padded shots then sit on its page background color. make_brand_kit makes one.

cover.description: The moment each place's cover shows, in seconds like "4.5" or as "0:04.5" (default: picked).

crop.description: A crop.json from plan_reframe or an earlier run, edited by hand: its windows are rendered as they are, and a shape it has none of is planned for its shots. It takes no cuts or steps, and no mode but fit.

cuts.description: Every shot change, in place of those found: seconds like 3.2,7.5, or a JSON file of seconds, of frames with their fps like {"fps": 30, "cuts": [96, 225]}, a launch film's film.timeline.json or a demo's steps.json.

for.description: The places, in one run at most 12: any of tiktok (1080x1920), reels (1080x1920), shorts (1080x1920), youtube (1920x1080), x (1920x1080), linkedin (1920x1080), feed (1080x1350, for the 4:5 feeds), square (1080x1080), all (every one of them, the default), or a size like 1080x1350, even sides of 64 to 4096 pixels from 1:4 to 4:1.

fps.description: The files' frame rate, like 30 or 29.97 (default: the video's own, within what the places take).

lufs.description: The loudness of every file in LUFS (default -14).

mode.description: follow crops each shot where what moves is, and pads a shot a crop would cut (default follow); center crops from the middle; pad shows every shot whole on a blurred copy or a color; fit keeps the picture's own shape and only fits each place's limits.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: <video-folder>/reframekit-<video-name>, where <video-name> is the name of video without its extension and <video-folder> is the folder video is in. A run replaces the files an earlier run of this kit left there, so give each version its own out_dir. The folder must be empty or hold an earlier run of this kit for the same video: any other folder stops it.

pad.description: What a padded shot sits on: blur (default, a blurred, darkened copy of itself), black, white, a color like #0f172a, or brand, the page background of the brand kit given as brand.

seconds.description: Keep at most this long in each place's video, cut at a shot change: seconds like "30", or "1:30".

steps.description: The steps.json of the demo this video is, when it is not beside the video under its name: it gives the pages, the page box and each click.

trim.description: Set to false never to cut a file to its place's length, for an account a place allows more, like TikTok's 10 minutes; FORMATS.md then says the file is over.

video.description: The finished video, any file ffmpeg reads, like film.mp4 from a launch film or demo.mp4 from a demo. The film.timeline.json or steps.json beside it, under its name, gives its shots.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

name: reframe_video

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.
